title: Best Antivirus Software 2026: 5 AVs Tested on Malware
description: Bitdefender, Norton 360, Malwarebytes, Microsoft Defender (free), Kaspersky — same Windows 11 PC, 1,000 real malware samples (recent + zero-day). Detection rate, false positives, system impact.
lede: Five antivirus solutions. Same Windows 11 PC. 1,000 real malware samples spanning recent ransomware, banking trojans, and zero-day variants. We measured detection rate, false-positive rate, and system slowdown.
methodology: Same Windows 11 machine (Core i5, 16GB RAM, NVMe SSD). Each AV given the 1,000-sample malware set (sourced from AV-TEST research feeds). Tracked detection rate, false positives on 500 legitimate executables, boot-time slowdown, file-copy slowdown.

sections.heading: Detection rate (the main number)
paragraphs: Detection on 1,000 recent malware samples: Bitdefender 99.7%, Norton 99.6%, Kaspersky 99.7%, Microsoft Defender 99.4%, Malwarebytes 98.2% (lower because it focuses on already-infected systems vs primary AV).
Zero-day samples (250 of the 1,000 were obfuscated/polymorphic): Bitdefender 98.8%, Norton 98.4%, Kaspersky 99.1%, Defender 96.8%, Malwarebytes 95.1%.
False positives on 500 legitimate executables: Defender 1 (best), Bitdefender 1, Norton 3, Kaspersky 2, Malwarebytes 5.

sections.heading: System impact
paragraphs: Boot-time slowdown vs no AV: Defender +2 sec, Bitdefender +4 sec, Kaspersky +5 sec, Norton +6 sec, Malwarebytes +3 sec.
File-copy slowdown (10GB folder): Defender +2%, Bitdefender +6%, Kaspersky +8%, Norton +12%, Malwarebytes +4%.
Daily idle CPU usage: all under 2%. Defender lowest at 0.4% idle CPU.

sections.heading: Beyond pure AV
paragraphs: VPN included: Norton 360 Deluxe (unlimited), Bitdefender (200MB/day limit), Kaspersky (no VPN), Malwarebytes (separate Privacy product), Defender (no VPN).
Identity theft monitoring: Norton 360 ($50k coverage), Bitdefender (US only, basic), others none.
Password manager: Norton, Bitdefender, Kaspersky include basic password managers. Use 1Password or Bitwarden instead — bundled password managers tend to be weaker.

faqs.a: For most home users on Windows 10/11 with cautious browsing habits: yes. Detection rate matches paid AVs, no separate install, zero cost. Where paid AVs win: identity theft monitoring, VPN bundles, family features.

faqs.q: Should I install Malwarebytes alongside another AV?
faqs.a: Yes — Malwarebytes is designed to coexist as a secondary scanner. It catches things primary AVs miss, especially PUPs and adware. Set Malwarebytes scan to weekly.

Kaspersky is technically excellent (one of the best detection rates), but the US federal government banned it from federal contracts in 2022 over national-security concerns. Individual users in the US can still use it; institutional risk and geopolitics may matter to you.

Bitdefender wins on raw detection + low system impact. Norton wins on bundled features (unlimited VPN, identity theft insurance, password manager). Pick by whether you want pure AV (Bitdefender) or AV+identity suite (Norton).

bitdefender-total-security.review: Bitdefender Total Security is the right paid pick for most users. 99.7% detection, lowest false-positive rate (tied), minimal system impact. Includes VPN (200MB/day, unlimited via Bitdefender Premium VPN add-on). 5 device licenses.
cons: VPN limited to 200MB/day on Total Security
Cyber Threat Intelligence dashboard isn't beginner-friendly

norton-360-deluxe.review: Norton 360 Deluxe is the right pick if you want AV + unlimited VPN + identity theft monitoring + password manager bundled. $50,000 identity theft insurance included. Higher system impact than Bitdefender but the bundled features are real value.
cons: Bundled password manager is weaker than 1Password

malwarebytes-premium.review: Malwarebytes Premium is the right pick as a SECONDARY scanner alongside your primary AV. Designed to catch PUPs (potentially unwanted programs), adware, and threats primary AVs miss. Real-time protection included.

windows-defender-free.review: Microsoft Defender (built-in Windows 10/11) is the right free pick for most home users. Detection rate matches paid AVs (99.4%), lowest false-positive rate, lowest system impact. No separate install. Free.

kaspersky-total-security.review: Kaspersky Total Security has top-tier detection (99.7%) and technical excellence. However, the US federal government banned Kaspersky from federal contracts in 2022 over national-security concerns about Russia-based operations. Individual US users can still use it; consider whether the geopolitical risk matters to you.
cons: Banned from US federal contracts since 2022

recommendedFor.label: Home users who want reliable free protection
recommendedFor.reason: Built into Windows 10/11 with 99.4% detection and the lowest system impact of all five — no install, no cost, no compromises for everyday browsing.

recommendedFor.label: Remote workers who use public Wi-Fi regularly
recommendedFor.reason: Unlimited VPN is bundled at no extra cost, plus $50k identity theft insurance — critical for anyone logging into work accounts on airport or cafe networks.

recommendedFor.label: Power users and developers running many executables
recommendedFor.reason: Tied for the lowest false-positive rate (just 1 hit on 500 legitimate files) and minimal system impact, so it won't interrupt builds or flag dev tools.

recommendedFor.label: Users who suspect an existing adware or PUP infection
recommendedFor.reason: Designed specifically to clean already-infected systems and runs alongside any primary AV, targeting PUPs and adware that other scanners routinely miss.

recommendedFor.label: Security researchers outside US federal environments
recommendedFor.reason: Best-in-class zero-day detection at 99.1% makes it a top technical choice for threat researchers willing to navigate the geopolitical trade-off.
